report_name: Ledger Hardware Wallet Supply Chain Attack Steals $90M+

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The attack involved compromising Ledger hardware wallets sold through the CryptoBilis reseller by physically tampering with the devices before they reached the customer.

attack_patterns.name: Hardware Additions
attack_patterns.description: Attackers physically modified Ledger devices to include an unauthorized hardware implant, which was used to steal the user's secret recovery phrase.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: The hardware implant was designed to steal the user's secret recovery phrase, which acts as the master credential for all their crypto assets, during the device setup process.

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used the stolen recovery phrases to import the victims' wallets and steal over $92.9 million in cryptocurrency from 311 wallets.

campaigns.name: CryptoBilis Supply Chain Attack
campaigns.description: A sophisticated supply chain attack targeting Ledger hardware wallets sold through the CryptoBilis reseller, involving physical tampering and hardware implants to steal cryptocurrency.

identities.name: Ledger
identities.description: A prominent manufacturer of cryptocurrency hardware wallets whose devices were targeted in a physical supply chain attack via an authorized reseller.

identities.name: CryptoBilis
identities.description: An authorized reseller of Ledger hardware wallets in Southeast Asia through which physically tampered devices were sold to customers.

infrastructure.name: Unauthorized Hardware Implant
infrastructure.description: A hidden hardware implant physically added to Ledger devices to intercept or exfiltrate the user's secret recovery phrase during device setup.
